Chess Armory Premium Checkers and Chess Set - Wooden Board Game with a Portable Wood Case and Secure Storage for Pieces, Set for Kids and Adults (Beech Wood) Chess has been my favorite board game for many, many years and I have a modest collection of chess sets. I do keep my eyes open for nice sets that are suitable for playing and travel. I selected this one because of the size - a little bigger than a typical travel set - and so far I have been very pleased with it.

Most travel sets I have seen and used have been small and of lower quality. There's nothing wrong with that, as you would not want to take an expensive set on the road unless traveling for the purpose of playing chess. This is a larger set, measuring 15"x15", which is suitable for play in most situations. It is not a tournament-sized set by any means, though.

I was mildly surprised by the fit and finish of this set. I say mildly because this is a more expensive set than many other travel sets, so I was expecting this to be a step up from typical travel sets though I wasn't expecting this much of a step up... The pieces are well made without rough spots or cuts and they're finished nicely so they're smooth. The board is also well-made and has a very smooth surface so that pieces can be slid without difficulty instead of having to pick them up and set them down again.

Also included is a set of checkers so that either game can be played on the board.

This is a better travel set than most, and it is larger than most I have seen too. It is well made and priced reasonably with the quality.
text_fidelity_b: Chess Armory Premium Checkers and Chess Set - Wooden Board Game with a Portable Wood Case and Secure Storage for Pieces, Set for Kids and Adults (Beech Wood)

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Track Builder Triple Loop Stunt Loops Hot Wheels 1:64 scale Vehicles [[VIDEOID:886df78722d87a8bdca79a9702180ce2]] This set is awesome!! There are a couple things to note about it that could be potential downsides/issues, if not prepared for-- but otherwise, everything is great! Below I will group the main points and for the 3 potential issues I'll mark it with this symbol:🔴 to hopefully make it easier to read through!

•We received all pieces included, and boxing, in great condition.

•1 car is included

•The quality of materials are true to Hot Wheels- great and sturdy plastic.

•It's a fairly easy set-up. My 9 year old put it together on her own by reading through the instructions step-by-step. It took around 30 minutes, may have been quicker but she often took short pauses, though she didn't need any help.

•There are about 3 different configurations you can do with this set. The video I posted shows each of these.

•Can connect to other Hot Wheels tracks and sets. (Including the colossal crash set that can be seen some in the background of the video I posted)

•Does not require batteries

•There are no levers that need to be reset for cars to go through the loops- my daughter has other loop sets that have those.

•You can set it up so that the launcher connects and starts at any of the loops. For example- you can connect the launcher to just the middle loop and the smallest. You can also try to launch it opposite- starting at the smallest loop and ending with the largest.

•You don't have to use the jumping ramps…you can have the cars finish the loops on a flat track.

🔴 One of the potential issues is the launcher- maybe it's just our launcher, or how we use it, but it can be a bit tricky to hit it with the right amount of pressure. Too hard and it knocks it off track. Too soft and it won't go around the loop. Sometimes it can take many tries and others it works right away. We have a few other types of launchers-- the long white one that is shown in the video I posted is the one she prefers to use since it seems to work better. Not everyone will have extra launchers, though. My daughter usually has no problem with trying multiple times with the one included in the set but I figured it's worth noting that it may not be a perfect launch each time.

🔴 The other possible issue are the cars used with it. You'll likely want at least a handful of different types of cars on hand, just in case. The one included does work pretty good. My daughter has a decent sized collection of cars and there a quite a few that often don't make it through the biggest loop. This could either be the car itself that doesn't work well or could also be an issue of the launcher (as just mentioned above). Some of her cars struggle on the biggest loop with the launcher provided- but when connected to the "stronger" launcher, they do great. And there's a few that still just don't make it. This could be an issue if this were very first set for a kiddo and if they have only 1 or 2 cars…just something to keep in mind if considering purchasing this set, you may want to consider also purchasing a handful of cars so that they can get the most use from it.

🔴 When you have it set-up as the Daredevil Jump or Gravity Drop, it sort of seems like the track isn't long enough since the cars shoot further past the cup a lot. So we added extra tracks (which aren't included in this set) and it helped a lot…the cars land in the cup more times than not. At the very end of the video I posted, you can see how we added an extra track to the Daredevil Jump set-up.

All-in-all: We love it! It keeps my 9 year old busy-- even if she doesn't connect it to her other tracks. She likes trying to get the cars in the cup and thinks that the triple loop feature is awesome.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Triple Loop Stunt Loops Hot Wheels 1:64 scale Vehicles

Just My Style Paint Your Own Mermaid Bank by Horizon Group USA. Paint & Decorate Your Own Coin Bank with Color Changing Sequin Decal & Metallic Holographic Paints, Blue Spoiler alert: what a fun group art project for a small group of children (or children at heart lol)! Great for siblings, sleepovers, or homeschoolers trying to squeeze in a fun extracurricular class :)

I have three girls ranging in ages 6 through almost 11, and ALL three of them enjoyed doing this project together (well, four if you include mom lol). My youngest painters (including one with autism) needed some manual assistance of course, but my 11 year old enjoyed working independently at her own level creating a more intricate design.

The quality of the tea set itself is the real deal: ceramic, and with proper (and of course gentle) care, this set should last long after the paint has cured (one page of simple--but important--instructions is included that tell you how to properly cure the paint after it has dried.)

Something I should point out to save some frustration: please realize that the unpainted ceramic arrives in a somewhat glossy finish... so that, when painted, the final finish will appear less like the picture of the tea set on the box, and more like an abstract watercolor design. Just something to keep in mind :)

Also, be sure to allow 24 hours for the paint to dry before curing it. Otherwise the color might appear weak. After completely dry, cure in the oven according to the included instructions. Allow to COOL COMPLETELY (preferably safely out of reach) and finally after a bit of patience...

VOILA! A lovely, top quality, and yes even CUSTOM tea set that may be enjoyed over and over again (my girls have already enjoyed several tea parties). A giftable winner!!

PopSockets Fidget Train with Expanding PopSockets , Premium Fidget Toy, ASMR, Toys for Adults and Kids I am a terrible fidget and I am always on the lookout for toys and gizmos that will keep me focused so I can sit still and not distract everyone around me. I selected this thinking it would be similar to those blister-type pop toys. It's not, but it's still an effective toy for stress relief and focus. It's possibly a little too noisy for a meeting, though.

At a glance this thing looks like the sections might come apart. They do not. Instead, this is an accordion-style fidget toy that you pull and push on the ends to make it expand and contract. It can be bent, twisted slightly, partially expanded and completely expanded. The colors are soothing and the tactile feel is nice.

When expanding the toy the sections are not silent. They're not loud, but they have a noticeable popping sound that's lost in the background in a normal environment but draws attention to itself in a more quiet area like a meeting room. It can be expanded more quietly with a little thought. If in an area where making a small amount of noise is acceptable, the sound is satisfying.

As I write this, this toy is close to $30 which seems high. This is really my only reservation with it.

I like this toy and will get some good use out of it. I usually mess with it when I am sitting at my desk and I want to sit still. It has a satisfying sound when popped, it's easy to work, and it looks pretty. It's a little on the expensive side, though.

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Super Tips Washable Markers Age 3+ - 50 Count I'll admit it: I'm an adult who loves to color. I find it a great way to relax, and there are some amazing "coloring books for adults" gaining popularity these days (Johanna Basford, Angie Grace, etc.). And there are whole communities of "colorists" popping up on social media.

So naturally, I'm looking for different mediums to use when I color. I've used colored pencils and gel pens, so I figured it was time to branch out into the marker arena. Someone suggested starting with these as they're water-based rather than alcohol-based, and Amazon has them at a good price, so I got the 50-ct set.

Overall, I'm pleased. There is a good selection of colors, several shades of each, which helps to bring some variety into th mix.

What I DON'T like (and this seems to be a problem for ALL coloring mediums): the actual color of the pen/pencil/etc. almost NEVER matches the color of the cap/barrel/etc. I realize that colors will look different depending on the type a "color" of paper used as the background, but seriously, some of these are WAY off. I find myself having to make a "cheat sheet" on the paper I'm using just so I can get a clear picture of how the various colors REALLY look.

Like I said, this isn't just a problem with Crayola, but they make it a little more difficult because the pens have NO distinguishing markings on them whatsoever to designate a color number or code. I ended up putting little pieces of masking tape on each pen and numbering them myself just so I can keep the color charts coordinated.

All that aside, they work great once you figure out the colors. Colors are vibrant, and I had very little "bleed through" or feathering in an Angie Grace book. Bleed through and feathering depend a great deal on the paper used, so bear that in mind and ALWAYS test before coloring.

Overall​, I like these - don't "love" them, but they're good quality water-based markers at a very good price.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Super Tips Washable Markers Age 3+ - 50 Count

Large Tumbling Timber Toy + Dice + Carry/Storage Bag - 54-Pc Wooden Blocks - Premium Pine Wood Floor Game for Kids & Adults - Grows from 1.5-feet to Almost 3-feet While Playing, Life Size Tower While many games make the claim that they are suitable for the whole family - this one is actually FUN for the whole family!

As most are familiar with the game Jenga, this is essentially played the same way - pull a block from the stack and place it on top. If your block causes the tower to tumble, you lose. The primary difference is the blocks are SUPERSIZED, measuring 7.1”(long) X 2.3”(wide) X 1.4”(tall). The blocks are the perfect size for little hands and kids get the hang of the game quickly and enjoy seeing the tower grow and eventually topple.

While the game’s tower begins at around 2’ it quickly grows to 4-5’+. The blocks are not only bigger but they are made of high grade pine, sanded smooth - 20 of the blocks are numbered (1-8, some numbers are duplicated while others are not) allowing players to develop a limitless number of custom games. Something we do is let the winner of each game write their name, or a short message on a block - it makes it fun to look back and remember the fun we have had during previews games.

In addition to the blocks this set comes complete with a wooden crate for storage and travel that easily doubles as a stable, flat playing surface when needed. In addition there is a white board with a dry erase marker for listing the rules you’ve set for the numbered blocks. Due to the 8 block being a one of a kind, we call it the Magic 8 Block and use that as a wild card type block - the person who pulls and places it can name whatever rule they choose.

This is a game reminiscent of games of old - no batteries, nothing electronic, it will last forever, can go anywhere to be played inside or out and is loads of fun for everyone.

This is most definitely a game set I recommend. We have loved it!

Playz Premium Solar System Model Kit for Kids - 4 Speed Motor, HD Planetarium Projector, 8 Painted Planets & 8 White Foam Balls with Paint and Brush for a Hands-On STEM DIY Project for Space Toys After my son and I finished this project, we were pretty underwhelmed. The price is $50, and that's on sale from $99? There is no way this thing should sell for $99, it's still a bit overpriced at $50. Some issues...

1. Our set came with 2 Saturn Arms, missing the Neptune arm. So we had to do a replacement with Amazon.

2. Inserting the pin rods in the planets, then into the arms. This was a pain. There is no way an 8 yr old would have been able to do this. I had to put on gloves to get a good grip to push the pins into the planets. Some of them, you hear a click, and some of them, you get no clicks no matter how hard you push.

3. The center projector that projects each planet is TERRIBLE. You need all the lights off, and you need the whole system to be close to the ceiling for you to see what planet its projecting. Out of focused and blurry. No way to focus it. The only way to get a sharper image is to put the project as close as possible to the wall.

4. Though the arms rotate around the sun, the individual planets do not rotate. So to explain night and day to your child, you'll need to manually rotate Earth. That would be asking too much, but hey, I thought this retails for $99? If they did charge $99, those planets better rotate by themselves. LOL!

3 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Playz Premium Solar System Model Kit for Kids - 4 Speed Motor, HD Planetarium Projector, 8 Painted Planets & 8 White Foam Balls with Paint and Brush for a Hands-On STEM DIY Project for Space Toys

BRICKKK Pantasy Building Block Set,Cute Building Kit Toys & Decoration (15100) Pantasy makes great building sets. The pieces stay together and the instructions are super clear.

This set consists of three sets of numbered bags, the instructions, and a small bonus sticker sheet. The stickers aren’t part of the set, but you could use them to decorate the planter pot.

The first two #1 bags build the planter, the three #2 bags build three succulents, and the three #3 bags build three more succulents and have round brown studs to simulate dirt.

I was a little wary of all the spiky pieces on the tall green succulent, but the pieces attach very well, I didn’t have a single loose one. All the other pieces stay together too.

The instructions are easy to follow. Some of the colors are dark and a little hard to see, but Pantasy outlines the new pieces for a step, which helps. They also give top-down views for steps like placing leaves or putting the succulents in the planter. I can’t remember that in any other instructions before, and I really liked it here. Very helpful.

I don’t like loose pieces, so I didn’t use the studs to mimic dirt. The planter is full without the studs, so I think that’s a matter of personal preference. The finished set fits right in with my other name-brand sets.

A visiting 5 years old boy, who is 44" tall, tried this chair and it fit him perfectly. His feet probably wouldn't have been flat on the ground if he'd been any shorter. The intended user is only ~2 years old, so she'll need to grow into it. Older children can, of course, fit it. The chairs are sturdy with 4 thick, wooden legs and a thick plastic seat and back made as one piece. When they arrive, there is some assembly. You simply screw the legs into the chair base, which was quick and simple to do. The chairs do wobble slightly on a flat (tile, concrete, wood) floor but are fine on even a thin carpet. You can unscrew a leg a little to stop the wobble if used on a flat floor. They have a pattern down one side of the back that you can see only when light hits it at certain angles. The chair is a solid off white color as the pattern is the same color as the rest of the chair.

The chairs can handle a maximum load of 154 pounds or 70 kg. They are intended for indoor use only. The chairs are intended for ages 3+. The chairs measure 11" from the floor to the seat and 26.5" from the floor to the top edge of the back. The seat measures 14.75" across and 11" deep. There is a 3.5" wide hand hole on the back that allows you to easily move the chair around. Overall, I expect the chairs to hold up to vigorous use.
text_fidelity_b: B. spaces by Battat - Kid Century Modern: Chair Set – Trendy Kid-Sized Furniture Set of Two Chairs in Plastic, Ivory

Rolife DIY Book Nook Kits Time Travel, 3D Wooden Puzzles Bookshelf Insert Decorative Bookend Model Kits with LED, DIY Crafts/Birthday Gifts/Home Decor for Girls&Boys Teens&Adults (Time Travel) I've seen these decorative bookends before, but they're rather pricey. So when I saw one that wasn't as expensive and looked like it would be a fun project, I decided to give it a try. I've always enjoyed crafts and a recent project was assembling and decorating an entire dollhouse.
That project, which took a couple of months, was nowhere near as frustrating as this, which took two days (when I'm determined, I'm determined).
Note that there's only ONE bookend in the kit. The first photo pictures two, but there's only one per kit. The kit comes with glue, a screwdriver, two lights, instructions, and everything you need except the batteries to power the lights. I would HIGHLY recommend that you provide a strong glue such as super glue or a really good wood glue for this project. You'll need it if my experience is anything to go by while building it.
I also recommend that you don't pop out the pieces beforehand, but do it while building (unless you are the type to label everything after you do that). There are a LOT of pieces to keep track of, and the labels aren't printed on them. Resist the temptation.
Now, for the kit itself. The instructions are NOT the best. There's 30+ pages, and very few words. It's basically illustrations and there were times when I feel steps were skipped. I had to figure out on my own which light when where (the shorter light for the door lamp, the longer one for the top light). Things like that. It was very frustrating.
Also, the kit is made out of a composite wood and has many, MANY tiny parts. Some parts that you have to push through tiny openings and through multiple openings. As careful as I was, these pieces broke. Hence the need for a really good, strong glue. The glue was also needed to keep pieces together. There were so many times that parts fell off when they shouldn't have, so gluing them together helped to move things along.
Oh, and I'd put pieces together only to have the instructions have pieces added later, and I'd be all 'why didn't they have me add this piece earlier'? Especially when you're pushing delicate pieces together.
If you've a miniature magnetic screwdriver, use it instead. The included screws are tiny and you're trying to get them in very small holes while screwing at awkward angles. Not having to worry about them falling will really help.
There was a lot of swearing involved with this project, I will not lie. I'm not sure this is a project for a kid, 14+ or older, unless they really like kit-building. Maybe if it was built out of better material. I debated what to rate it, but since it turned out looking good in the end (with the help of a lot of extra glue), I went with three stars. The finished product is lovely and the lights work, it was just very frustrating to get there.
text_fidelity_b: Rolife DIY Book Nook Kits Time Travel, 3D Wooden Puzzles Bookshelf Insert Decorative Bookend Model Kits with LED, DIY Crafts/Birthday Gifts/Home Decor for Girls&Boys Teens&Adults (Time Travel)

text_fidelity_a:
Wonder Forge Marvel I Can Do That! Game We also have this game in the Dr. Seuss theme, and they're both fun. They're very similar in both cards and directions, but this one is great for little fans of Marvel.

There's a note on the directions page to let you know it's fine to customize the rules for your family. (We tend to do that anyway, but it's a great reminder!) There are 3 stacks of numbered/colored cards(1-red, 2-blue, 3-green). The player turns over one card from each stack. They'll tell the player what to do with which objects. For example, the first card will tell you to "Do a push-up". The second card: "with Captain Marvel's energy ball", and the third card: "on your head". Some tasks are harder than others! Each card will get a certain amount of stars. (At the end of the game, the players will add the stars up. The player with the most wins.) If your child thinks he/she can do the specified task, they will say, "I Can Do That!" If not, they can exchange a card at a time until they feel they can do the task. One of my children was given the task of "Crab walk under the portal, with Spider-Man's web, between your elbows". None of us were talented enough to do that, so he picked again. This is also a great escape route for the shyer(or younger) little ones. Some things will be less embarrassing or more doable for them than others.

There are also "Battle" cards. If one of those are drawn, then any other cards drawn will be put back in the mix. The player will then try to knock down the Green Goblin card with the object specified on the card. If the task is completed, the card is set aside. If not, the player has to put that card in his/her pile as a reminder to discard 2 cards before counting stars at the end of the game. (That way, they can discard to 2 with the lowest number of stars.)

While it may get old with what the players do, it does create a variety of mix and match tasks. The cards are constantly being shuffled. The game ends when all the cards are gone.

This is a great game for when movement is needed. It's not one that the players just sit around and play. The players have to get up and move around. There's also a nice variety of types of objects. There's a plastic block that will need to be filled with air, along with a ball(that's already aired up). There's foam items and thick cardboard objects(Green Goblin and Captain America's shield). My biggest complaint is the "portal". This isn't the sturdiest of things. It's hard to get it to stand up straight, mainly because it has to be rolled up a bit to fit in the box. It makes it hard to get under at times. The bigger/older the child, the harder it will be to crawl under it, either way. This is definitely a game for littler/younger people. Also, I fear that the block won't last long, since objects that require air don't make it too long around my home, in general. (For it to fit back in the box after each game, the air will have to be released. That means you'll have to blow it up before each game. It's not huge, so it's not the biggest deal. Particularly if used in a classroom setting, though, germs/cleaning wipes would be something to put into consideration.)

My children(3, 5, and a tiny 8) have really enjoyed playing this game, though!
text_fidelity_b: Wonder Forge Marvel I Can Do That! Game

Lucky Ducks - The Memory and Matching Game That Moves - Includes A Fun Pop The Pig Make-A-Match Card Game The only bad thing about this game is the fact that my 2 year thinks it's a radio. We've had it for about a month now, and as I write this, it's "playing" in the background. It's playing in the background almost every night, if not during the day, too. It's super annoying! :P It's supposed to sound like ducks, I guess, but it's just lots of squeaking.

Otherwise, it's super cute, and my boys love playing it. I think 2-4 year old children will enjoy it the most, but it's labeled 3 and up. I imagine this is due to the stickers that must go on the ducks, and game board(which is a motorized pond). You do need batteries! There are 4 colors of stickers, 4 each. 3 of each will go on ducks and 1 on the game board. I wasn't paying attention enough to realize one of each color went on the game board. I ended up having to peel some stickers off of ducks.

You put the ducks on the game board, assign a color to each child(up to 4 players), and then press the center button. The ducks will then circle around the pond. Taking turns the child picks up a duck and turns it over. If it matches their assigned color, they keep it. If not, they put it back on the pond. While all the ducks are on the pond, it's a little crowded, so it was tough for my 2 year old to get the duck placed back on there without knocking over another duck, or several. It's easier to turn the pond off while your child is looking at the color and placing it back on the pond.

Overall, this is a fun game to teach a few colors, along with the art of taking turns and patience. My children had so much fun with it, they were impatient for their turn.
text_fidelity_b: Lucky Ducks - The Memory and Matching Game That Moves - Includes A Fun Pop The Pig Make-A-Match Card Game

My Critter Catcher - Spider and Insect Catcher So I know that spiders are generally good, in that they eat other bugs. But they are also terrifying because they are FAST and HIDE BEHIND THINGS, just waiting to attack! Trying to remove them with a cup and piece of paper is perilous at best (what if it GETS OUT and gets on my hand?? I would flail in terror and then who knows where it would land?). So, to defend myself from these miniature terrors, I bought this.

I knew my time had come when my cats were staring at the floor. It was my nemesis, a spider. I tore the catcher out of the packaging and - with only a little shrieking - successfully subdued the spider! It was caught in the bristles, unable to escape! And I was at a safe distance, unlike the cup method where I'd be practically touching the spider. I darted outside and released it. I told the spider he was evicted and to eat bugs outside, never inside. If it ever does venture inside aagin, I know my cat sentries would alert me to its presence and - with minimal shrieking - I could safely evict it again.

MACTANO The Great Wave Micro Building Blocks Set for Adult Kanagawa Surfs Waves Home Decor Model Toys Building Kit -2296PCS This is a set of 3 succulent planter pots, each mini set is bagged separately with its pieces and instructions.

The bags for each mini set are unnumbered, you’ll need to open all at the start. All of them except the bags of round 1x1 plates. The studs are meant to simulate dirt, and you don’t attach them to anything, simply pour them in the pots. I didn’t use the studs, the pots are really full and I couldn’t see the bases anyway.

The pieces mostly stay together on the succulents themselves. But some of the pieces are loose, especially the connections between succulent and pot. To build the sets, you assemble the various succulents and then attach them inside the pot. Most of the succulents clip into the base with bar pieces. Imagine a piece that looks like: —C. Sometimes those clips didn’t hold very well, so sticking a second succulent in was enough to dislodge the first.

Getting all the succulents inside each pot takes some finessing and patience. The finished sets are display pieces, not for play -- they are a bit delicate.

The instructions are usually easy to understand, though sometimes I did have to go back or flip forward to understand where a piece went. Some of the colors are off. For example, dark pink in the instructions are really orange pieces. The color differences made some of the sets harder than others, since I couldn’t always tell which piece to use.

I did like that the set include extra stamen options. Getting to choose my own flower colors among the options, or even mix them, was fun.

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Juniors/4+ Jurassic World Pteranodon Escape 10756 Building Kit (84 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This summer was the year of Jurassic World! My 5 turning 6 year old is too young to watch any of the Jurassic Park movies, but that didn't stop the advertisements and displays in stores from reaching audiences far and wide including my son. He already loves Legos AND dinosaurs so this was the perfect mashup for him! We already have other Lego Juniors sets (I honestly wish they would make more).

Lego Juniors are designed for 4-7 year olds. Basically, they are the same as the other Lego kits, but the instructions are more simplistic than the other kits for older children. The Legos designs are also more simple than the Lego kits for older children. The Legos are still the same size as regular Legos, so these are not an in between Duplos and Legos. If you step on them they will hurt. In addition, the pieces are tiny enough to get lost forever.

My son is a free form builder, he does not care about the actual instructions, what he cares about is the potential for creating what is shown on the package. His Lego bin is filled with Lego kits all mixed together and he has a blast creating his own world, which is limitless. So, if you are insistent on your child following the directions to a T, then I would not recommend these for a younger child. Most boys under 6 just do not have the patience for this. Frustration sets in quick and the desire to just play take over. Stick to Duplos or just plain free build sets until about age 6 or 7 if you want to stick to the instructions. However, if you don't mind the kits getting mixed up for creative play and you child loves Legos and Dinos, then this is the set for you.

As usual, the Legos are of the same quality we had when we were kids. I would recommend getting several of the Lego tools because some of this pieces are tiny and get stuck. The only way to get them out is via the Lego Tool!
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Juniors/4+ Jurassic World Pteranodon Escape 10756 Building Kit (84 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Fallout The Board Game (Base) | Strategy | Apocalyptic Adventure Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14 and up | 1 to 4 Players | Average Playtime 2-3 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games From the first time I saw Fallout the board game on the shelf I knew I wanted it. I have been a fan of the Fallout line since the first game. I have play almost every Fallout video game to come out and it was time to get the board game. After watching a couple videos on how to play, I was very intimidated. There seemed to be a lot of moving parts, card decks and miniatures. My fiancé and I play a most of our games together and I was thinking this would be one that would be a little out of her comfort zone.

I played through the single player game mode and enjoyed the game from the start. After the first game I knew the game was not as complicated as I thought. The game was so fun I stayed up till 3 am playing the game another 2 times. The next day I set it up for my fiancé and I, and I wasn’t disappointed. My favorite part of the game is the questing. The flavor and the ways you go about completing the quest feel like playing a video game. This is the closet I have come, in a board game, to a video game RPG. With hundreds of quest cards, the game replay is awesome. We both enjoyed the game and can’t wait to introduce it to our play group.

I play a lot of tabletop games with miniature and the piece in Fallout are top quality. Before long they will be painted and looking great on the great design of the game tiles. It really feels like you are in the wastelands. For those of you that have played the games, look forward to the quest for the Wasteland Survival Guide! All of the cards are well designed and I really like the decks are different physical sizes. There wasn’t enough room in the box for the insert and all the cards/game pieces. And there was not enough bags for all the game pieces, packaging could have been thought out a little more. Other than that, the game is great and I am looking forward to the expansion.
text_fidelity_b: Fallout The Board Game (Base) | Strategy | Apocalyptic Adventure Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14 and up | 1 to 4 Players | Average Playtime 2-3 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Empire State Building 216 Piece 3D Jigsaw Puzzle for Kids and Adults - Easy Click Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly We hit a Waterloo at piece 181 that took days to get past. For some reason the peices became much harder to put in all at once. There are dividers taht happen whenever the building reaches a ledge, and this was one such point. Oddly, it was harder than the rest. The easily frustrated might be tempted to shove it in a box in the darkest part of the deepest closet and pretend it didn't happen. Those who enjoy putting the same twelve pieces in 6,000 times until it sticks will find this absolutely delightful. So not for beginning model builders, but nice for intermediate and advanced. Probably also good for advanced beginner.

It isn't a puzzle in the classic sense. The instructions tell you how many peices to put in, and you put them in by following the numbers. Then you get an embellishment and another group of numbers. It's a model that provides the appearance of a jigsaw.

Overall, I had a lot of fun with it, the resulting model was beautiful, and even though it's sitting on top of an out of the way bookcase, it's gotten many compliments.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Empire State Building 216 Piece 3D Jigsaw Puzzle for Kids and Adults - Easy Click Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly

text_fidelity_a: Crayola 18ct Twistables Colored Pencils (2 Pack) These twistable pencils came in superb packaging and thus arrived in great condition, none broken, pencils and their boxes in excellent condition. They are more portable in that you don't have to always carry a pencil sharpener or worry about emptying shavings. These are excellent for children and also for seniors or anyone who doesn't have a lot of strength in their hands, or who struggles with sharpening pencils. Bomber Lures Who Dat Spoon Spinner Bait Fishing Lure The Bomber Saltwater Grade "Who Dat" Rattling Spinner Spoon - Gold tone from Bomber is a 3" long gold painted spoon like luer with a large 5/0 sized plated hook. It has a guard with a swiveled gold spinner at then end of the plastic and is attached with a screw, which could be removed. When fished for larger saltwater fish, it is a little bit bulkier than the usual spoon, in that is made with a rattling cavity "throat" at the eye end of the body up front to give it a hefty weight forward look. The rattling heard when holding the hook and swivel to keep them from moving is a low pitched clicking rattle. The size of this specific hook is comparable to a 5/0 Strike King hook and it weighed 0.84 ounce on my digital scale. The sound and wobbling, clicking and spinner flash may intimidate a finicky feeding smaller fish, but this luer will only make a big Bull Red Drum hungrier. Big Specs also should not be scared of this spoon and the shiny gold spoon is a proven offering for both redfish and trout. Bomber has offered a uniquely designed product with the Who Dat Rattling Spinner Spoon and the later reviews from buyers will determine if it will catch fish. Good luck with it and enjoy your next day fishing.

I took pictures with my phone and have tried to add them to the product pictures, haven't seen them yet.

text_fidelity_a: Marvel Captain America Disc Launching Shield When I saw this product was available, I thought that I would order it for my 10 year old son, who wants to see the movie Captain America when it is released later this summer. After receiving it, I asked him to write a review from the perspective of a 10-year-old. This is what he had to say: "The Captain America Shield is really fun. It is easy to put together(he literally read the directions and assembled the parts all by himself). I just had to add 4 batteries and place the foam discs in it. When you shoot the discs you hear a sound, like a siren. But the sound can get kind of annoying. Other than that, the shield is pretty fun". From a parents perspective, I thought that (1) the easy to read instructions allows kids to problem solve and work independently. (2) The sound when the discs are fired acts as a warning system (kind of a fail safe although I don't think the foam discs could cause any damage). And if a child ever accidentally fired the discs in the direction of another child's eyes, although I don't think that they will be injured, they will at least hear it coming. (3) The armband and handgrip are perfect for holding the shield. And (4) it seems like fun. While my 10 year old (it was his birthday today) had fun, I do think that a slightly younger child (7 or 8) would have more fun and not become bored as quickly as an older one.
text_fidelity_b: Marvel Captain America Disc Launching Shield

I don't want to go into detailed description, but this so-called "toy" is not something a kid will play with, regardless of age. It includes several square magnets, some round magnets, a couple of rubber ribbon magnets, a nail, a couple of wooden blocks, some pieces of plastic and that's basically it. The manual includes some "activities", which basically represent instructions like "put magnet A on magnet B and see they repel. turn them over and now they attract. wow! now let's go to the next activity". All of those activities require extra stuff such as coins, bricks, sticky tape, strings, and even contact cement, which is not included in the box.

Doesn't worth a dime. Seriously.

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Toy Car Track Set Hill Climb Champion with 1:64 Scale Car, Launch Uphill to Score Points & Win Amazon was temporarily out of stock so I grabbed this from another source. We are an avid Hot Wheels family and always like to check out the newer sets. I love the idea of running a car around a course continuously, without relying on batteries. This set comes with a big launcher, that features a unique track with protruding tabs that catch the cars from behind as you blast them around the track. The whole idea is to catch the car(s) at the right time when it reenters the launcher, so you can have it racing around the course non-stop. Unfortunately, the course is too small and uninteresting, yet, if the layout was much larger, that launcher wouldn't have enough force without some kind of midway helper (like an automatic loop launcher). This would make a world of a difference in fun, so you you're not pounding the launcher every half second to keep the car circulating around a tiny oval which gets old fast.

Big annoyance: The launcher is very tall, so it comes in packed in two pieces which easily lock together, however, once locked, you're unable to seperate them. This is now the second set we have with this annoying problem. We like storing our hot wheels in their boxes, but once opened, there's no way to get this giant launcher back inside. Even if storing out of the box, with other toys, it's a big jalopy that could have been dismantled, taking up less space.

And finally, kids need laser-sharp hand/eye coordination to catch the car on time, so this may frustrate the impatient type. When you do manage to catch the car to keep it going, it does feel rewarding, even if it's only 2 laps. We haven't tried more than one car at a time, but I imagine on a large course, it must be fun, but on this small circuit, it's probably near impossible to work with.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Toy Car Track Set Hill Climb Champion with 1:64 Scale Car, Launch Uphill to Score Points & Win

GK Galleria Frozen 2 Birthday Party Supplies for 12 Princesses with 170 Plus Items - Birthday Party Supplies - Frozen Party Decorations - Frozen Plates and Tablecloth - Anna Olaf Elsa Impressive shower head at an impressive price. Let's break it down...

** IN THE BOX ** Along with the showerhead there is a small roll of teflon thread tape, rubber pipe gasket, in-pipe flow restrictor, and instructions.

** INSTALLATION ** Remove old shower head. Clean pipe threads. Apply 3 turns of pipe thread in a CLOCKWISE direction. Extend shower head extension pipe arm all the way out. If you want flow restriction, insert now, other insert pipe gasket. Attach shower head in a CLOCKWISE direction by hand until tight. Cover the plastic thread cap (nearest the pipe) with a cloth and tighten 1/4 turn with a pliers or pipe wrench using GENTLE pressure. The shower head can now be straightened by gentle turning the adjustment screw (nearest shower head) by hand. It will click. Once you have the general downward direction of the shower head placed, test for leaks. If it leaks at the pipe & shower head connection, gently tighten another 1/4 turn. Once you're ready you can position the shower head, by head, any which way you like . It will click letting you know it's locked.

** USAGE ** Turn water on to your favorite temperature and insert your glorious naked self under the shower head. Look up at the nipples. Yes, there are 90 nipples up there. Very supple nipples that can be squeezed for cleaning. With so many nipples I don't think I'm ever leaving the shower ever again. The 90 nipples provided me an even pressurized rain all over my smelly carcass.

** THOUGHTS ** The TH2.5 works like a charm. Big, even rain all over me. Just what I wanted. Installation was simple provided you have normal shower pipes and are a bit handy with some pliers. The joints articulate well with no movement once set. The joints, once set, should accommodate short and tall humans. I'm 6'1", the wild redhead is 5'7" so this head works amazingly well for both of us. Did I mention there were 90 nipples?

** POINTS OF INTEREST **
- flow is optional and NOT installed
- joints articulate with a solid 'click' and stay in place
- pipe tape and gasket are included
- cover with cloth during final tightening to avoid scratching
- gently squeeze the nipples to clean
- looks like the USS Enterprise from the side... Aye, Aye Captain!
- I just love saying the word 'nipples'
text_fidelity_b: GK Galleria Frozen 2 Birthday Party Supplies for 12 Princesses with 170 Plus Items - Birthday Party Supplies - Frozen Party Decorations - Frozen Plates and Tablecloth - Anna Olaf Elsa

Klutz Felted Friends Craft Kit I purchased this for my cousin's daughter, who at six is considerably below the age recommended. In terms of skill I think she can handle the assembly instructions - one might object on the grounds of the pokey-stabby tool used for the felting, and while she did poke herself a couple times during the install, her parents fared considerably worse.

Speaking of which; she produced a fuzzy friend (the bunny - purple, to be specific) within an hour of trying. The project went well, though her father managed to break two of the needles during the trial-and-error phase, so I'll have to replace those. She seemed to have some fun with it, especially since she was able to assemble the bunny with her parents. There is also a certain amount of observation involved - you have to watch and learn the art of felting, which I think is a good experience for a kid; obviously it didn't take too long, but then my sister was also assisting and she knows all about material/felt/stitching/quiliting and that sort of stuff.

Overall, I would say it makes a good gift. It is, as described, easy to get into and produces a walnut to kiwi-sized fuzzy animal with maybe thirty-minutes of actual work. Probably best for kids over the age of six, though.

Would recommend for gifting to first cousins once-removed.
